extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for a performer's delivery—use of intonation, rhythm, cadence, tempo, and pauses—to build expectation, heighten payoff, and manage audience reaction in live comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing builds expectation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pace can change the meaning of a joke. Great timing allows listeners to create expectations. Comedy = introducing expectation, then subverting. Timing manipulates the expectation curve. Note: Faster ≠ better; slower can be either devastating or boring depending on intent and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pregnant pause before payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a pregnant pause before the payoff?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'pregnant pause' is pausing just before the payoff word — 'pregnant' because it promises to deliver. It builds tension that releases at the punch. Sometimes the pause itself can be the joke (famous example: Jack Benny holding silence when asked his age).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow audience reaction time
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comedian allow audience reaction time?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pause after the punchline to let the audience process and laugh; don't step on your own laughs. 'Hold' when needed for the audience to catch up. Allowing reaction preserves the tension/laughter relationship: laughter releases tension that the pause has built.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm consistent yet surprising
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the rhythm consistent yet surprising?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use intonation, rhythm, cadence, tempo, and beat to guide the comedic narrative. Maintain a recognizable rhythm so listeners form expectations, but introduce surprises (timing shifts or beats) to subvert those expectations and generate laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery matches the joke's emotional shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the delivery match the joke's emotional shape?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match speed and tone to the joke's emotional weight: slow down for drama, weight, or a final reveal; speed up for absurdity, patter, or list jokes. Delivery should reinforce the intended emotional arc of the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempo selection appropriate to content
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the chosen tempo (faster vs. slower) appropriate to the joke?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that pace can change meaning. Faster pacing can create absurdity or energy but may swamp subtlety; slower pacing can heighten impact but risks boredom if overused. Choose tempo deliberately to serve the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other timing tools (speed up / slow down / hold / cut off)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the performer employ timing tools—speed up, slow down, hold, or cut off—effectively?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speed up for absurdity/patter/list jokes. Slow down for drama/weight/final reveal. Hold for the audience to catch up. 'Cut off' audience laughter strategically to keep them wanting more, but be careful not to alienate the room. These tools are tactical ways to shape anticipation and release.
